Save This Pontiac: 1967 Car Needs a Complete Restoration, Work Under Way
45 photos
Photo: eBay seller johnnblevin1
Runs and drives but still needs work. This is the essential information you need to know about this 1967 Pontiac, as the car is here because it needs a new owner willing to pick up from where its restoration work was suspended.
This isn’t the most desirable Pontiac, but it still makes for a fantastic daily driver if you’re in the market for an affordable project.
The restoration work has already started, but the seller didn’t share additional information as to whether they wanted to keep this Pontiac original or go for a custom build that just works.
Photo: eBay seller johnnblevin1 The Tempest family included multiple choices, including the Custom convertible, the Custom 4-door hardtop, and the Custom Sports Coupe, but Pontiac used every opportunity to brag about its new lineup of wagons.
The GM brand used its marketing papers to highlight the low price of its wagons, despite the impressive lineup of features installed at no extra cost.
“Our new Tempest Safari is unquestionably the most elegant wagon ever to grace the low-price field,” Pontiac said. “We turned our stylists and engineers loose on this one, and they came up with things like walnut wood grain styled panels, thick nylon blend carpeting, and all Morrokide interior, plus a revolutionary overhead cam 6 engine.”
It worked. The Tempest was a successful model, despite not selling in the big numbers that Pontiac hoped and certainly not becoming as desirable as other models, such as the GTO .
It also didn’t get the powerful engines on the GTO, as the focus was on building an affordable model whose focus was also on economy.
The standard choice was a 230 six with only 165 horsepower, while a similar version of this engine but with a higher compression ratio, a four-barrel carburetor, and running on premium fuel increased the output to 215 horsepower.
If you wanted V8 power, the first option was a 326 with 250 horsepower. It sported a two-barrel carburetor. The HO version dropped the two-barrel for a four-barrel and used a dual-exhaust system to produce 285 horsepower. This engine was not available on station wagons, so the highest you could go on a Tempest wagon was the regular version of the 326.
Photo: eBay seller johnnblevin1 This Tempest still has an engine under the hood, and the good news is that it starts and runs. “It will go into drive and reverse,” the seller explains, but that’s all the good news end. The car needs urgent work, and its stopping power is very limited at this point.
“The fuel tank will hold about a quarter tank but has been patched with fuel tank epoxy over a small pinhole,” the seller notes.
My recommendation is that you go there in person to inspect this Pontiac if you are interested in buying the car, especially if you don’t live far away and the travel costs wouldn’t be too high.
The metal appears to be in decent condition, though the car already sports some patches on the floor. “The frame seems solid,” the owner explains, but you’ll find rust around the trunk. Some bondo repairs have already been made.
Photo: eBay seller johnnblevin1 This Pontiac Tempest is a solid project, but it’s pretty clear that this car is not supposed to be a collectible or anything similar. It’s an honest restoration candidate, and I doubt that anyone would buy this car to keep it original and turn it into an occasional driver. If anything, it makes more sense as a daily driver, especially considering the V8 under the hood.
The selling price is always the one that makes a huge difference between a vehicle that would stay where it is for much longer or a restoration candidate that eventually receives this long overdue refresh.
Fortunately, this Tempest isn’t at all expensive, and that’s why many people have decided to add it to their watchlists. There are 18 people who decided to keep an eye on this Pontiac, and there’s a good chance more users will save the listing once it gets more exposure.
The owner wants $4,200 for this Pontiac, but they also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay. This means other offers would also be considered, but there’s no guarantee the price would drop significantly. However, I don’t expect any offer below $4,000 to be accepted, but you should be able to discuss all these details on the phone or during your live inspection.
The vehicle is parked in Berea, Kentucky, and considering the engine has seen better days and the stopping power isn’t the best, you should also bring transportation to take the car home. You still have 11 days to figure out if you should buy the car, but you’d better make a decision as fast as possible because someone else might trigger the BIN option at any moment.
A clean title is also available for the buyer, but no other papers are offered.
